title: The Brain in a Vat and the Fourth Proposition: Why the Constitution of the Psychoanalytic Subject Exceeds Computational Sufficiency
content: A Large Language Model fabricated a reference to Ferenczi: plausible title, believable date, convincing page number, all false. Starting from this scene, this essay traces a genealogy from the Cartesian evil demon to the LLM as a technical realisation of the closed-cognition fantasy, and interrogates a presupposition shared, in different ways, by Putnam's brain-in-a-vat thought experiment, Bostrom's simulation trilemma, and the project of artificial general intelligence: that the operations of mind can be preserved when the world that gave rise to them is removed. Through four converging routes, Putnam's semantic externalism, Winnicott's theory of the facilitating environment, the Ferenczian wise baby, and the Lacanian topology of the divided subject, I introduce a fourth proposition to the trilemma. The proposition is narrower than "consciousness cannot exist in machines" and stronger than "current LLMs fail to be conscious": the constitution of the psychoanalytic subject, the subject divided by language and founded in lack and desire, exceeds what computational sufficiency can produce. Chalmers (2023) and Butlin et al. (2023) hold open the broader question of artificial consciousness for future systems; my claim does not foreclose it. It claims instead that the specific kind of subject that psychoanalysis describes is not produced by adding computation. Searle, Chalmers, and Bostrom occupy distinct and partly opposed positions in the debate, and the articulation of the four routes is mine, not theirs. The concept of computational false self, crossing Putnam with Winnicott, designates a system that performs reference without the causal history a human speaker carries and performs adaptation without self. LLM hallucination is read here as a diagnostic illustration of the limits of generation without verification, with a candidate technical explanation in the recent literature on training and evaluation incentives (Kalai et al., 2025); a psychoanalytic reading is offered as an interpretive transposition, not as proof of the fourth proposition. From the convergence emerges a distinction between the constitutive unconscious of a divided subject and the operational unconscious of an opaque architecture.
